title: Any-Order Flexible Length Masked Diffusion
claim: Existing masked diffusion can only unmask within a fixed-length sequence; ours also inserts new tokens, giving variable length while keeping any-order generation.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels (MDM left, FlexMDM right) with top-to-bottom time steps t=0 to t=1, a legend inset at top right, and a ✗/✓ capability row along the bottom
description: Two side-by-side panels compare MDM (left) and FlexMDM (right). Each panel shows token sequences as rows of colored boxes, running from t=0 at the top to t=1 at the bottom, with dotted ellipses between steps. The rows are labeled X_0, X_s, X_u and X_1 in the center. In MDM, six tan 'mask' boxes gradually turn into blue words ('I love blue skies green cows') at a fixed length. A blue box f_θ(X_s,s)[i] with an arrow shows unmasking. In FlexMDM, the sequence starts from one empty box and grows. Teal 'mask' boxes are inserted, and a teal box g_θ(X_s,s)[j] marks the insertion step. Blue boxes mark unmasking, and the final sentence includes the new word 'Rio's'. A legend at top right defines Inserted (teal), Unmasked (blue) and Empty (white). A bottom row shows red ✗ marks for MDM's Variable Length and Token Insertion, and green ✓ marks for FlexMDM.
caption: Flexible Masked Diffusion Model (FlexMDM) addresses MDMs’ inability to handle variable-length sequences and token insertion while preserving any-order generation power. At each step, FlexMDM performs \textbf{\xxgreen{insertion}} and \textbf{\xblue{unmasking}} by predicting \xxgreen{the expected number of mask tokens to insert ($g_\theta$)} and the \xblue{posterior over clean tokens ($f_\theta$)}, respectively.
abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models over discrete domains. MDMs generate sequences in an any-order, parallel fashion, enabling fast inference and strong performance on non-causal tasks. However, a crucial limitation is that they do not support token insertions and are thus limited to fixed-length generations. To this end, we introduce Flexible Masked Diffusion Models (FlexMDMs), a discrete diffusion paradigm that simultaneously can model sequences of flexible length while provably retaining MDMs' flexibility of any-order inference. Grounded in an extension of the stochastic interpolant framework, FlexMDMs generate sequences by inserting mask tokens and unmasking them. Empirically, we show that FlexMDMs match MDMs in perplexity while modeling length statistics with much higher fidelity. On a synthetic maze planning task, they achieve $\approx 60 \%$ higher success rate than MDM baselines. Finally, we show pretrained MDMs can easily be retrofitted into FlexMDMs: on 16 H100s, it takes only three days to fine-tune LLaDA-8B into a FlexMDM, achieving superior performance on math (GSM8K, $58\% \to 67\%$) and code infilling performance ($52\% \to 65\%$).
